intro: Speech-language pathology assistants teach, encourage and track progress, skills shared with therapy assistant and education roles. The closest of the 25 careers below is Occupational Therapy Assistants, with a 91% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $72,300.
why_it_works: Each session means following a treatment plan, practicing speech and language exercises and noting small improvements for the pathologist. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 3.5 out of 5 for this job and service orientation at 3.38. Occupational and physical therapy assisting, psychiatric care and special education use the same patience and care. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page lists medians.
tips: Speech-Language Pathologists earn $97,870 but need a graduate degree and license.
Physical Therapist Assistants earn $68,380 and are an 82% match after an associate program.
Special education teaching is a 77% match with a median of $74,260, though it needs a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: What jobs can former speech-language pathology assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Occupational Therapy Assistants (91%), Psychiatric Technicians (87%) and occupational therapy aides (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Physical Therapist Assistants are 82% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $68,380 for hands-on rehabilitation work.

faq.q: Which jobs for speech-language pathology assistants pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Speech-Language Pathologists at $97,870, adapted physical education specialists at $76,580 and secondary special education teachers at $74,260, according to BLS May 2025 data. All three need more education than the assistant role.

faq.q: Do speech-language pathology assistants need more education to switch?
faq.a: Often. 13 of the 25 matches need no more education than these assistants already have, including 8 of the top 10, while 1 needs a graduate degree. An associate degree is common, held by 92% of workers in the closest match.

faq.q: What skills should speech-language pathology assistants build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are troubleshooting, managing people, quality control analysis and coordination. Complex problem solving already rates 3.25 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so clinical judgment and planning are the main steps toward licensed roles.
